subject: science
passage: Many of the chemical reactions that sustain life would proceed far too slowly to be useful at body temperature if left to themselves. Enzymes accelerate these reactions, sometimes by factors of many millions, by holding the reacting molecules in positions that lower the energy needed to transform them. Crucially, an enzyme emerges from each reaction chemically unchanged, so a single enzyme molecule can ______ the same transformation thousands of times. This is why cells need only small quantities of most enzymes to keep their metabolism running.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: An enzyme speeds up a reaction and "emerges from each reaction chemically unchanged," so it can speed up the same reaction again and again. To speed up a reaction without being used up is to "catalyze" it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Enzymes "accelerate" reactions, so they do not inhibit, or slow, them.
explanation.B: Correct. A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being changed itself, so one enzyme molecule can catalyze the same reaction many times.
explanation.C: Incorrect. To counteract a transformation is to work against it, but enzymes help reactions happen faster.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The enzyme does not undergo the transformation; it comes out "chemically unchanged." The reacting molecules are what get transformed.
